European NATO Military Spending, 2014–2025

Author

Edward McKelvey

Published

September 28, 2026

Summary

In 2025, 21 of 29 European NATO members spent at least 2% of GDP on their militaries, up from 2 in 2014. Poland stands out, reaching 4.5% of GDP, well above NATO’s new 3.5% core target. Germany has roughly doubled its share since 2014, to 2.3%, while the UK is at 2.4%.

Data and method

Data come from the SIPRI Military Expenditure Database (2026 release). The analysis covers the 29 European NATO members with armed forces; Iceland is excluded because it has none. SIPRI and NATO define military spending differently, so these figures will not always match NATO’s official estimates.

All figures in this report are generated from code. See the project README for how to reproduce it.
